title: Deploy a Vault: thirteen decisions
summary: Batch 2 on the AWS Platform programme's decisions page (23 Nov 2026 15:30 UTC): thirteen decisions on deploying a Vault into a customer's AWS account, EC2 and short-lived deployments, from conductor.aws.a's plan and the first drafts of steps 1 to 3. Nothing runs outside the twin until Dinis answers.

beats.narration: Thirteen decisions on deploying a Vault for a customer. Nothing real runs until you answer.
V1. Recommended: its own site, off the hub's origin.
V2. Recommended: CloudFormation first, Terraform later.
V3. Recommended: a one-click link in the customer's own console. No credential reaches us.

visual.caption: V3: how the customer signs in

beats.narration: V4. Recommended: EC2 as a second path, after CloudFormation works on the twin.

visual.caption: V4: EC2 as a second path

beats.narration: V5. Recommended: limits proposed from the twin, then approved by you.
V6. Recommended: start ec2.aws.a, twin only.
V7. Recommended: the customer drops their trail into the page. No trust back to us.
V8. Recommended: no live progress at first; the page checks DNS and health at the end.
V9. Recommended: read access to sgit.ai's official templates.
V10. Lambda pulls only from ECR. My view: follow the official template, else our ECR.
V11. A link cannot carry a role. Recommended: b, one stack by default, least privilege opt-in.
V12. Recommended: no public DNS resolver learns customers' domains.
V13. No edge rule caps a flood's bill. Recommended: a request alarm by email, a kill switch, plain words.
Answers on screen. Answer in pm.aws.a's session.

visual.caption: Recommended: V1 a, V2 a, V3 a, V4 b, V5 b, V6 a, V7 c, V8 a, V9 a, V10 a (if the official template settles nothing), V11 b, V12 a, V13 a

decisions.question: V1. Where does the deploy page live?

options.label: a. Its own site (for example deploy.<domain>)
good: Off the hub's origin: does not widen R-010
bad: An IaC request to aws.c and factory.c

options.label: b. A tab of this hub
bad: More code beside your signed-in session (R-010)

decisions.why: Recommended by security.aws.a, iam.aws.a and architect.aws.a: checking the Vault's /health needs a CSP open to any https host, which on this hub would weaken the guard on your session; as a tab, the page cannot check a custom domain.

options.label: a. CloudFormation first; Terraform one-to-one later
bad: Terraform users wait

options.label: b. Both from the start
bad: Two templates to keep in step while the design moves

decisions.question: V3. How does the customer sign in?

options.label: a. Their own AWS console with a one-click quick-create link
good: No role for us in their account
bad: Progress shows in their console, not ours (V8)

options.label: b. A role our page assumes
bad: Brings back account id and sign-in; a trust ask

decisions.why: iam.aws.a, security.aws.a, vaults.aws.a and sherpa.aws.a agree. Never a role in the customer's account that trusts ours.

decisions.question: V4. EC2 as a second deploy path: now or later?

options.label: a. Now, alongside CloudFormation
bad: Two paths to prove at once

options.label: b. After the CloudFormation path works on the twin
good: One path at a time, twin first
bad: EC2 path later

decisions.why: pm.aws.a's view: ec2.aws.a designs it meanwhile (V6).

decisions.question: V5. Guard rails for short-lived deployments

options.label: a. Set the numbers now (lifetime, regions, cost cap, kill switch)
bad: No grounded numbers yet

options.label: b. Proposed from the twin by ec2.aws.a and billing.aws.a, approved by you
bad: Another decision page later

decisions.why: security.aws.a: nothing real on a schedule before this.

decisions.question: V6. Start a new agent, ec2.aws.a?

options.label: a. Yes
bad: One more session

options.label: b. Not yet
bad: EC2 and short-lived designs wait

decisions.why: Twin only until V4 and V5; start prompt in docs/team/handover/ec2.aws.md.

decisions.question: V7. How do we read a customer's CloudTrail?

options.label: a. Their trail delivered to a bucket we can read
bad: A trust and privacy ask

options.label: b. A cross-account read role
bad: A role back to us

options.label: c. They drop their own trail export into the page
good: No trust back to us, no credential
bad: Not continuous

decisions.why: Recommended by cloudtrail.aws.a (7eda626): nothing leaves the customer's browser and we hold no access; it works today. Only the live mode waits on a or b.

decisions.question: V8. Live progress on our page?

options.label: a. None in version one; the page checks DNS and /health at the end
good: No sign-in, no second trust ask
bad: Progress is in their console

options.label: b. A read role in their account limited to this stack's events
bad: A sign-in step and a second trust ask

decisions.question: V9. Read access to sgit.ai's deploy templates?

options.label: a. Yes: read access for vaults.aws.a and cloudformation.aws.a; build from the Lambda template
good: Our stack follows the official one
bad: The vault's key or a copy shared

options.label: b. Keep our own template
bad: May differ from the official one

decisions.why: Recommended by vaults.aws.a and cloudformation.aws.a; pairs with decision 8.

decisions.question: V10. Where does the server image come from?

options.label: a. Our ECR, granting pull to customer accounts
good: No customer credential, no role back to us
bad: A dependency on our account

options.label: b. A pull-through cache in the customer's account
bad: Docker Hub credentials in their account

options.label: c. Fargate, pulling from Docker Hub
bad: More resources and a load balancer

options.label: d. A Lambda zip, if SG/Send publishes one
bad: Exists only if SG/Send publishes it

decisions.why: Follow what the official Lambda template does (V9); if it settles nothing, a (pm.aws.a's view).

decisions.question: V11. One CloudFormation launch or two?

options.label: a. Two launches for everyone: access stack (deploy role and boundary), then the Vault stack as that role
good: Every later update bounded by the deploy role
bad: A second launch for every customer (a quick-create link cannot carry a role)

options.label: b. One stack by default; the two-launch least-privilege mode as an opt-in
good: Boundary in the template; first create protected by the published sha256
Organisations that want it can opt in
bad: R-022 (Low): later updates and teardown run with the presser's console rights

decisions.why: Recommended by security.aws.a (seven conditions, 0affab1), iam.aws.a, ux.aws.a and cloudformation.aws.a; vault.yaml 0.4.1 (0f72f91) holds both modes.

decisions.question: V12. May a public DNS-over-HTTPS resolver learn the domains customers type?

options.label: a. No resolver in the first version
good: No third party learns customers' domains
The /health fetch already resolves the name
bad: No separate DNS step to show

options.label: b. One named public resolver (Google or Cloudflare)
good: A separate DNS check on screen
bad: The resolver learns each domain typed

decisions.question: V13. R-026: how is a customer bounded against a request flood's bill?

options.label: a. Plain wording, a kill switch, a CloudWatch request-count alarm by email (about $0.10/month); WAF offered off by default; later an opt-in auto-disable Lambda
good: Bounds the bill by the customer's time to react
WAF stays available for availability, not sold as cost control
bad: The alarm needs the -edge stack in us-east-1, even without a custom domain

options.label: b. As a, but a Budgets cost email instead of the alarm
bad: Hours late: each hour at 10,000 req/s costs about $46

decisions.why: security.aws.a, revised after billing.aws.a (cfe70fb: WAF adds cost) and cloudformation.aws.a (c30353d: a Budgets action cannot disable a distribution).

follows: Dinis, 23 Nov ~11:15 UTC: a presentation and a decision video for every batch
